text:
Seoul’s autumn nights took on a club-like atmosphere Sunday as about 2,000 people gathered at Mount Nam in the center of the capital for a silent DJ party — where dancers tune into live sets through wireless headphones rather than loudspeakers — turning one of the city’s best-known scenic spots into an open-air dance floor.
The event, dubbed Palgak Club, closed out the inaugural 2026 Namsan Night Festival, an initiative by the Seoul Metropolitan Government to expand nighttime leisure options and draw more visitors to surrounding neighborhoods.
At Mount Nam Palgakjeong Plaza on Sunday, the headphone-driven format let crowds dance to live DJs without blasting music over conventional speakers, cutting down on noise complaints around the hillside landmark.
The event ran in two sessions, from 5:30 p.m. to 7 p.m. and from 7:30 p.m. to 9 p.m., with music spanning several genres and participants adjusting headphone volumes to suit their preferences.
The city distributed LED glow bracelets and luminous temporary tattoo stickers, adding color to the illuminated plaza as families, couples and groups of friends joined the festivities.
Safety personnel managed pedestrian traffic, while additional Mount Nam circular buses were deployed to help visitors return home, the city said.
Palgak Club followed several other festival programs held since October, including Namsan Campnic, an outdoor camping-themed event at Baekbeom Square that sold out shortly after reservations opened, and Autumn Foliage Walks connecting mountain trails with nearby neighborhoods such as Haebangchon, Itaewon, Chungmuro and Euljiro.
A survey of 1,329 participants in the earlier programs found that 93.9 percent were satisfied with the festival overall, while 95.1 percent said they intended to attend next year.
Namsan Campnic received a satisfaction rating of 98.1 percent, while Autumn Foliage Walks scored 91.3 percent.
The survey also found that 95.5 percent of respondents had used or planned to use nearby businesses or delivery services, suggesting the festival helped stimulate spending in surrounding commercial districts.
Kim Young-hwan, head of the Seoul Metropolitan Government’s Garden and Urban Parks Bureau, said the city appreciated the strong public response to its first festival of this kind.
“We thank the many citizens and tourists who joined this new event, introduced this year to offer a distinctive way to enjoy Namsan’s nighttime scenery,” Kim said.
“We will present a variety of nighttime programs reflecting Namsan’s unique appeal at the 2027 Namsan Night Festival."
This article was published with the assistance of generative AI and edited by The Korea Times.
